items.b: That's the number. A plain apartment — not luxury, not a view of anything, just four walls you're allowed to lock — costs about thirty thousand dollars.
That's what a shop clerk takes home in a month. It's also roughly what a guy selling socks in the bazaar clears. Same number, same stomach-drop on the 1st.

items.t: 250 months
items.b: Divide them. Save every single dollar and eat nothing, and you'd own that apartment in 250 months. That's twenty years of not spending on anything, ever.

items.t: But you do eat
items.b: Which is the part everyone forgets when they do this math on paper with a nice round number and a smile.

items.t: Half is already gone
items.b: Take away food, bus fare, and the phone bill, and you're maybe setting aside $50 a month. Now it's 600 months. Fifty years.

items.t: Fifty years
items.b: Start at twenty, finish at seventy. You'd be signing for your front door the year your back gives out.

items.t: That's not a savings plan
items.b: That's a life sentence with a balcony.

items.t: "Just work harder"
items.b: Sure. Except there's a ceiling on how many hours a body can be awake, and the math doesn't care how motivated you are about it.

items.t: The bazaar guy isn't lazy
items.b: He opens at seven, closes at nine, six days a week. He's not behind because he slacked. He's behind because the numbers were never on his side.

items.t: One hour of his life
items.b: $120 across roughly 200 working hours comes out to about sixty cents an hour. Read that again and then tell someone to hustle.

items.t: A meal costs four hours
items.b: Call it three dollars for something basic on the street. At that wage, dinner is four hours of your life traded for dinner.

items.t: The teacher's month
items.b: Often less than $120. A person trusted with other people's kids, doing it for less than a phone bill in most countries.

items.t: Rent eats the rest
items.b: Not everyone even gets to start saving. Rent in a decent city quietly consumes the fifty dollars you were going to keep.

items.t: The car costs more than the apartment
items.b: Read that a second time. In a country that manufactures little you'd want, a basic car can out-price a home.

items.t: Inflation isn't a shock, it's weather
items.b: Prices don't jump once. They creep. You don't wake up to a disaster, you wake up to a slow drip you already got used to.

items.t: Nobody plans to be poor here
items.b: They plan. They budget. They skip the fruit. And the plan still breaks, every single month, in the same place.

items.t: The word is "squeezed"
items.b: Not crashed. Not collapsed. Squeezed — slowly, politely, with a smile and a receipt.

items.t: Two different realities
items.b: The number in your account says fine. The number at the store says otherwise. Only one of those is yours to spend.

items.t: "Just move abroad"
items.b: It costs money to leave. The cheapest flight out is more than a full month of the income we're talking about.

items.t: The ones who left worked three jobs
items.b: Not because they're smarter. Because they ran the exact same hustle inside an economy that actually pays for it.

items.t: A haircut is a decision now
items.b: Not a big one. Just a decision with a number attached, and you make it with your teeth clenched a little.

items.t: Nobody posts this part
items.b: Instagram shows the trip up north. It doesn't show the forty-seven days of instant noodles that paid for it.

items.t: The cruelest bit: everyone knows
items.b: There's no illusion left. You're not misinformed, you're just stuck. That's a completely different kind of hard.

items.t: This is not a complaint, it's division
items.b: Two numbers were handed over: thirty thousand, and one-twenty. Everything above is just what happens when you divide one by the other.

items.t: You're reading this from somewhere else
items.b: Which means for once, you're standing outside this particular math. That's not luck you should sit on. Don't waste the position.

title: THE BIOLOGY OF YOU
subtitle: Where your opinions actually come from.

items.t: You started as one cell
items.b: Not a person. Not a plan. One cell — no opinions, no name, no idea what was coming.

items.t: Then it split
items.b: Two. And the entire game changed, because two cells have to coordinate, and coordination needs instructions.

items.t: The instructions are a gene
items.b: Not a personality. Not a destiny. A molecule with exactly two priorities: keep me, copy me.

items.t: Keep me. Copy me.
items.b: That's the whole brief. Every human ambition you've ever watched is downstream of something that just wants a backup copy.

items.t: You're the strategy, not the strategist
items.b: You didn't decide to want things. Wanting arrived already attached to you, already running, no setup required.

items.t: Why you don't feel like a colony
items.b: Because the coordination is invisible. Thirty-seven trillion cells agreeing on "I'm hungry" feels exactly like one thought.

items.t: You are literally a truce
items.b: Your body is a ceasefire between cells that all want slightly different things. It works. Most days.

items.t: "Alone" is a feeling, not a fact
items.b: Nothing in you is solitary. Even your gut is a city of other organisms with their own agenda.

items.t: The biology version of not alone
items.b: Every cell in you is running the same deal, struck 3.8 billion years ago. You're a very loud branch of one very old argument.

items.t: Replication isn't romantic
items.b: It isn't about legacy or meaning. It's a pattern that made more of itself — and the patterns that didn't, aren't here to be sad about it.

items.t: Survivorship, that's all
items.b: You're not the best design. You're the design that happened to still be running when everyone else's version stopped.

items.t: So why does it feel like meaning?
items.b: Because a pattern that doesn't protect itself stops existing. Meaning is the alarm bell, not the reason for the alarm.

items.t: Anger is a price tag
items.b: When you rage at being cut off in traffic, that's your brain slapping a value on something and screaming THIS MATTERS. You didn't set that value. It came pre-installed.

items.t: Jealousy is a spreadsheet entry
items.b: Your code logged "resources held by others = threat to my copy." You just get to feel it as a knot somewhere under your ribs.

items.t: Fear is maintenance
items.b: The thing keeping you alive never asked your permission and has no interest in whether you find it exhausting.

items.t: You never chose your first preference
items.b: You showed up already preferring sugar over dirt, warm over cold, safe over unsafe. All of it arrived with the package.

items.t: Even your opinions have a boss
items.b: The things you're certain about feel like yours. Trace them back far enough and you'll hit machinery you never built.

items.t: This doesn't make you a robot
items.b: Knowing the wiring doesn't switch it off. You still get to look at the alarm and decide what to do next.

items.t: That's actually the upgrade
items.b: A cell can't overrule its drives. You can notice one, name it, and pick anyway. Nothing before you could do that.

items.t: The line nobody drew
items.b: Somewhere between one cell and a person who reads, the pattern learned to argue with itself. That's us. That's the strange part.

items.t: What you are now is the receipt
items.b: Every ancestor who survived a winter, a drought, one bad decision — you're the final line item on a very long invoice.

items.t: A running total
items.b: Not a miracle. Just an unbroken chain of good enough, again, again, again, with no days off.

items.t: The chain doesn't care about your bad day
items.b: It handed you a nervous system and moved on. What you build with it is genuinely, uncomfortably, up to you.

items.t: Blame the gene, then get up
items.b: Knowing emotions are installed doesn't make them fake. It makes them editable. That's a better deal than most people get.

items.t: 3.8 billion years landed on you opening this card
items.b: Statistically absurd. Might as well do something loud with it.

title: YOU GOT A SEAT
subtitle: The rarest thing in the cosmos, and you're holding it.

items.t: Infinite people never got here
items.b: Every line that ended, every person who never reproduced, every road that just stopped. You're the exception, not the rule.

items.t: And infinite more won't
items.b: People who'll never be born because of a choice made in the next five minutes. You're not late. You're not early. You're exactly here.

items.t: The seat was almost not yours
items.b: One different decision by one ancestor and you're a different person, or no person at all.

items.t: You're alive right now
items.b: Not in a postcard way. Actually. While you read this, you're one of the tiny fraction of everything that can notice anything.

items.t: The universe is 13.8 billion years old
items.b: It waited that long to build something that could look back at it. That something is currently you, on a screen, slightly bored.

items.t: You can taste things
items.b: A structure made of stardust figured out how to detect sugar. Nothing else up there has that feature.

items.t: You can get bored
items.b: Complaining about boredom is a luxury problem. Rocks don't get bored. Neither does 99.9999% of everything that exists.

items.t: You can miss people
items.b: Missing requires memory, which requires a brain that bothered to store something. Amazing machine, terrible billing department.

items.t: Someone laughed at something you said once
items.b: You probably don't remember it. They might. That's a real event in a real universe, caused directly by you.

items.t: The weather is free
items.b: Not money-free. Just: nobody charged you for the color of that sunset, and it still happened anyway.

items.t: You have a tomorrow
items.b: Not guaranteed, but scheduled. Most things that ever existed had no schedule at all, not even a rough one.

items.t: You can change your mind
items.b: Genuinely. A single cell can't. A rock can't. You can read one card and walk away different than you arrived.

items.t: Someone from 500 years ago would call you a god
items.b: Running water, a light you switch on with your finger, food from three continents. You've been bored of miracles for years.

items.t: You're bored of miracles
items.b: Let that land properly. You got handed the impossible and filed it under "Tuesday, nothing special."

items.t: You can choose what to think about next
items.b: That wasn't always on. For most of history, most people got one job and one set of rules and no say in the matter.

items.t: You're not starving while reading this
items.b: If you are — eat first, come back. If you're not, that's one problem already solved today. Check.

items.t: You have access to every book ever written
items.b: In your pocket, for free. And we mostly use it to watch a stranger fall off a chair.

items.t: That's still your right
items.b: Nobody has to earn the right to waste an afternoon. Sometimes wasting the afternoon is the entire point of the afternoon.

items.t: You can be kind on purpose
items.b: Instinct gets you some of it. Doing it when it's inconvenient — that's the part no gene ever asked for.

items.t: You can forgive a gene
items.b: Yours is running on very old code with a very short memory. Knowing that makes you the adult in the room.

items.t: The people after you aren't born yet
items.b: Someone in 2140 will exist because of something you do or don't do. You're not a passenger. You're the hinge.

items.t: Someone before you gave up something for you
items.b: A name you'll never know stayed alive long enough for your line to continue. They get no credit. You are the credit.

items.t: It cost 13.8 billion years to get you here
items.b: That's the bill on the table. Try not to undersell the product.

items.t: Nobody's handing out medals for existing
items.b: Which is strange, because existing was genuinely the hard part. Everything after that is negotiable.

items.t: So what are you doing with it?
items.b: Not a demand. Just a real question. You've got the rarest thing in the cosmos and it's on a timer.

title: GLAD YOU'RE NOT THIS
subtitle: One specific animal. No human wants its job.

items.t: The tapeworm
items.b: No mouth. No stomach. No eyes. No brain. It lives in the dark inside another creature and absorbs whatever it's given. It's been doing this for 500 million years.

items.t: That's the bar
items.b: Half a billion years of what we'd call "success," and it has never once gotten to see anything at all.

items.t: It has no idea it exists
items.b: And honestly, neither do you most days. The difference is that you get to notice that, which is somehow worse and way better.

items.t: Nobody wrote a poem about a tapeworm
items.b: And it wouldn't matter if they did. There's no one in there to read it.

items.t: Its whole life is someone else's lunch
items.b: It never picked a meal, a room, a name. It just arrived inside a system and did the only thing it knows how to do.

items.t: Survival with zero enjoyment
items.b: You say life is hard. A tapeworm couldn't understand the complaint, or the concept of "better," or the word "worse."

items.t: And it's still winning
items.b: It outlived the dinosaurs. It'll probably outlive us. Which should tell you that winning was never the point.

items.t: Now the parasitic wasp
items.b: It stings a caterpillar, paralyzes it, lays eggs inside, and the eggs hatch and eat the host from the inside out. Alive. In order.

items.t: That's a Tuesday for it
items.b: No villain. No plan. Just a program running with the brightness turned all the way off.

items.t: The botfly larva
items.b: Burrows into skin, eats its way around, comes out when it's finished. You'd be screaming the entire time. It wouldn't be.

items.t: The male anglerfish
items.b: He bites the female, fuses to her, dissolves, and becomes nothing but a pair of gonads. That's the entire career path.

items.t: Koala fingerprints
items.b: Under a microscope they're indistinguishable from a human's. Evolution ran out of ideas and copied ours. Nobody asked permission.

items.t: Your cat would eat you if you stopped moving
items.b: Not out of malice. Its "care" setting simply doesn't cover you. You are not in the config file.

items.t: The point isn't "it's worse out there"
items.b: The point is: you got the version with eyes, jokes, cold drinks, and the ability to be annoyed by all three.

items.t: You can be sad. They can't even get that far.
items.b: Sadness requires a self to be sad about. Most living things never make it as far as having a self.

items.t: Being miserable is an upgrade
items.b: Read that again with a straight face. It means you have something to lose, which is not a small thing.

items.t: A rock isn't depressed
items.b: It also isn't anything. The minimum entry fee for being anything at all is that you sometimes feel bad about it.

items.t: The tapeworm can't have a bad day
items.b: It also can't have a good one. That's the trade it made by not bothering with a brain.

items.t: You get both
items.b: Good day, bad day, weird day, day you refuse to describe to anyone. Both columns come with the same membership.

items.t: Nobody has ever envied a jellyfish
items.b: No brain, no heart, no blood. It drifts. It's extremely good at drifting. Still not what anyone's aiming for.

items.t: Consider the sponge
items.b: It doesn't eat, think, move, or notice anything. It's been at this for 600 million years. Not one person is jealous.

items.t: Glad you're not that?
items.b: Then you already answered what you'd rather be instead. Hold onto that answer, it's more useful than it looks.

items.t: Every alternative on the table is worse
items.b: That's not a reason to be smug. It's a reason to stop renegotiating with your own life.

items.t: You drew the only hand that can complain about the hand
items.b: Which is either the universe's best joke or its entire point, and nobody's confirming which.

items.t: So no, you don't want to be a tapeworm
items.b: Good. Now go act like somebody who knows exactly what they dodged.

title: NOW GO
subtitle: The part where you do something.

items.t: The gene doesn't care how you feel
items.b: Good news. Neither should you, about the excuses you've been rehearsing.

items.t: Motivation is a guest, not a tenant
items.b: It'll visit sometimes. Don't hand it the lease. Do the work while it's out of the house.

items.t: Start embarrassingly small
items.b: Two minutes. One sentence. One push-up. The bar has to be low enough that arguing with it looks stupid.

items.t: Nobody's coming
items.b: Not a mentor, not a moment, not a sign from the universe. The only sign you're getting is the one you build yourself.

items.t: The discomfort is the whole product
items.b: Everything you want is sitting on the other side of something you don't want to do. Every time.

items.t: You're allowed to be bad at it
items.b: For a while. Being bad at something is just the entry fee, and everybody pays it in full, upfront.

items.t: Discipline beats feelings
items.b: Feelings change four times before lunch. Discipline is just feelings that agreed to show up anyway.

items.t: Your ancestors survived worse with less
items.b: A famine, a war, a winter with no heater. Your excuse is a push notification.

items.t: Comparison is a rigged game
items.b: You're putting your chapter two next to their chapter twenty, using their highlight reel as the ruler.

items.t: Stop negotiating with 6 a.m.
items.b: Decide the night before. The morning version of you is not to be trusted with anything important.

items.t: Boredom is a superpower
items.b: Can't sit still anymore? Nobody can. The one person who still can is going to take all of it.

items.t: Do the boring thing unimpressively
items.b: Not perfectly, not with a color-coded planner. Just done, badly, again tomorrow. That's the whole method.

items.t: You don't need a breakthrough
items.b: You need four hundred unremarkable days in a row and the willingness to not be excited about most of them.

items.t: The work is the reward
items.b: Not eventually, actually. The day you stop dreading it is the exact day it starts paying you back.

items.t: You're behind on a clock you invented
items.b: There's no schedule. There's no deadline. There's just people who started and people who are still thinking about it.

items.t: Nobody's keeping score
items.b: Which is both freeing and terrifying. Nobody will notice if you quit. That's exactly why you shouldn't.

items.t: Quitting is quiet
items.b: Success makes noise. Failure just closes a tab one afternoon and nobody ever asks what happened there.

items.t: Make it stupidly easy to start
items.b: Shoes by the door. Document already open. Remove the friction and you remove most of the argument.

items.t: Track it or it didn't happen
items.b: One line a day. You'll hate the empty days far more than you hate the actual work.

items.t: Rest is part of the plan
items.b: Not a betrayal of the plan. A machine that never stops isn't dedicated — it's just broken and hasn't told anyone.

items.t: Your mood is weather
items.b: It passes whether you argue with it or not. Work through it and it becomes just a Tuesday that happened to rain.

items.t: Feel it and do it anyway
items.b: That's not suppression, that's adulthood. The fear stays exactly where it is. You move regardless.

items.t: Five years from now is coming either way
items.b: You'll arrive at it no matter what you do. Might as well have something to show for the trip.

items.t: The you of next year is watching
items.b: Not mystically. Just practically — they're either going to be grateful or annoyed, and you're the only one who picks which.

items.t: You're the only person who can
items.b: Not the most talented, not the most connected. Just the only one with your exact access to right now.

title: LOOSE THOUGHTS
subtitle: Things that don't fit anywhere else.

items.t: Everyone's improvising
items.b: Nobody has it figured out. Some people are just better at performing that they do, and it's mostly just performance.

items.t: "Normal" is the average of everyone's worst days
items.b: You're comparing your behind-the-scenes to a number that nobody ever agreed to in the first place.

items.t: Time is the only thing you can't earn back
items.b: You'll trade money for it every single time you're sick. Might be worth acting like you believe that.

items.t: You've already survived your worst day
items.b: Statistically, your record is 100%. Perfect. Nobody's beaten it yet.

items.t: Most of what you're worried about won't happen
items.b: The rest you'll handle, because you always have, with zero notice and no preparation whatsoever.

items.t: You are not your best idea
items.b: Or your worst one. You're the one standing there deciding which one gets built.

items.t: Nobody thinks about you as much as you do
items.b: Slightly freeing. Slightly insulting. Both are true at the same time and that's fine.

items.t: The thing you're avoiding takes four minutes
items.b: It's been four hours of avoiding it. That ratio is the entire problem, in one line.

items.t: "Someday" is not a date
items.b: It's a rejection letter you wrote to yourself and never sent, so it doesn't even feel like one.

items.t: You can start over
items.b: Not from zero — you keep the skills and the scars — but you can absolutely start again.

items.t: Kindness is free and rarely on sale
items.b: Because nobody's marketing it. There's no campaign. Do it anyway, it's the cheapest thing that moves people.

items.t: The people who annoy you most are running old code too
items.b: Same as you, slightly different install date, fewer updates applied.

items.t: You'll forget 90% of this week
items.b: Which is either horrifying or an extremely generous feature, depending on the week you're having.

items.t: A bad ten minutes isn't a bad life
items.b: It's ten minutes. Your brain just turns the volume all the way up and calls it permanent.

items.t: Money is a tool with terrible marketing
items.b: Everyone thinks it's the destination. It's a hammer. Stop trying to eat the hammer.

items.t: You don't need more time, you need fewer tabs
items.b: In your browser and in your head, and honestly mostly in your head.

items.t: The fastest way to feel better is to move
items.b: Walk. Not a metaphor. Actually walk, ten minutes, outside. The chemistry does the rest of the job for you.

items.t: Nobody claps for the things you didn't do
items.b: Including you. Go do exactly one of them and see how the day changes.

items.t: Your taste is better than your skills
items.b: Good. That gap is where all of the interesting work lives, and it's the only sign you need that you're progressing.

items.t: Boring people are made, not born
items.b: They just stopped asking questions somewhere around thirty. Don't stop asking questions.

items.t: You're allowed to outgrow people
items.b: Not with drama, not with a speech. Just quietly, while walking in a slightly different direction.

items.t: The phone will still be there
items.b: It's been ninety minutes of scrolling and you'd genuinely struggle to name three things you saw in it.

items.t: Say the thing
items.b: To them, to yourself, out loud. Half of life is unspoken and all of it is heavy to carry around alone.

items.t: One day this will be a memory with a weird smell
items.b: And you'll wish you'd been a lot less tense about it while it was actually happening.

items.t: You're doing better than the tapeworm
items.b: Which, if you think about it for two seconds, was the bar all along.
